Model 3: Inverse-Probability-Weighted Normal Niche (Horvitz--Thompson)

Source: vignettes/model_ip_weighted.Rmd
model_ip_weighted.Rmd

1 Ecological Motivation

When the environmental conditions available in the accessible area MM are unevenly distributed, a naive maximum-likelihood estimate of the niche centroid μ\mu is biased toward whatever environments happen to be common in MM. For example, if 70 % of MM has temperature near 15 °C, the presence-only MLE will be pulled toward 15 °C even if the species tolerates a wider or differently centred range.

The inverse-probability-weighted (IPW) model removes this environmental-availability confound by reweighting each background point by the inverse of its local environmental density w(𝐱)=1/ĝ(𝐱)w(\mathbf{x}) = 1/\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}). This converts the discrete sum over the heterogeneous background grid into a numerical approximation of a Lebesgue-measure integral, effectively projecting the niche onto a uniform environmental space.

This is a Horvitz–Thompson (HT) estimator (Horvitz and Thompson (1952)) applied to the restricted likelihood framework of Jimenez et al. (2019).

2 Data-Generating Process

2.1 The Jimenez DGP

The IPW model assumes the Jimenez et al. (2019) DGP: presences are drawn from the fundamental niche density f(𝐱;μ,Σ)f(\mathbf{x};\mu,\Sigma)restricted to the set of environments that exist in MM:

p(𝐱i∣presence in M)=f(𝐱i;μ,Σ)∫Mf(𝐱;μ,Σ)d𝐱. p(\mathbf{x}_i \mid \text{presence in } M) = \frac{f(\mathbf{x}_i;\mu,\Sigma)} {\int_M f(\mathbf{x};\mu,\Sigma)\,d\mathbf{x}}. \tag{1}

Under this DGP the observation probability at environment 𝐱\mathbf{x} depends only on the species’ intrinsic tolerance, not on how common 𝐱\mathbf{x} is in MM. This is appropriate when:

  • Sampling effort is approximately uniform across MM (e.g. systematic surveys).
  • The analyst explicitly wants to estimate the fundamental niche (Hutchinson 1957), not the realised niche shaped by MM.

2.2 Contrast with the Use-Availability DGP

The "weighted" model (Model 2) assumes instead that presence intensity ∝f⋅g\propto f \cdot g. The two DGPs yield different estimands:

DGP Weight Estimand
Jimenez (this model) w=1/ĝw = 1/\hat{g} Fundamental niche on uniform EE-space
Use-availability (Model 2) w=ĝw = \hat{g} Niche under MM-biased observation

Neither is universally “correct”; the choice depends on the ecological question and the data-collection protocol.

3 Mathematical Specification

3.1 Restricted Log-Likelihood

Starting from Equation 8 of Jimenez and Soberón (2022) with w=1/ĝw = 1/\hat{g}:

ℓ(μ,Σ)=∑i=1nlog⁡f(𝐱i)−∑i=1nlog⁡ĝ(𝐱i)−nlog⁡∑j=1Kf(𝐲j)ĝ(𝐲j). \ell(\mu,\Sigma) = \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log f(\mathbf{x}_i) - \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i) - n\,\log\!\sum_{j=1}^{K}\frac{f(\mathbf{y}_j)}{\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)}. \tag{2}

3.2 Negative Log-Likelihood (Minimised Objective)

Substituting f=𝒩(μ,Σ)f = \mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma) and dropping the (2π)−p/2(2\pi)^{-p/2} constant (which cancels between numerator and denominator):

−ℓ*(θ)=12∑i=1nqi+∑i=1nlog⁡ĝ(𝐱i)+n⋅logsumexp⁡j[−12qj−logĝ(𝐲j)], -\ell^*(\theta) = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n} q_i + \sum_{i=1}^{n}\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i) + n\cdot\operatorname{logsumexp}_j\!\left[ -\tfrac{1}{2}q_j - \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) \right], \tag{3}

where qi=∥L−1(𝐱i−μ)∥2q_i = \|L^{-1}(\mathbf{x}_i - \mu)\|^2 (squared Mahalanobis distance), qjq_j is the same quantity at background point 𝐲j\mathbf{y}_j, and ĝ(⋅)\hat{g}(\cdot) is the Gaussian KDE evaluated at the point.

3.3 Sign Convention (vs. Weighted)

Term "weighted" (Eq. 8, w=ĝw = \hat{g}) "ip_weighted" (Eq. 8, w=1/ĝw = 1/\hat{g})
Numerator KDE −∑ilog⁡ĝ(𝐱i)-\sum_i \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i) +∑ilog⁡ĝ(𝐱i)+\sum_i \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{x}_i)
Denominator integrand +log⁡ĝ(𝐲j)−12qj+\log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) - \frac{1}{2}q_j −12qj−log⁡ĝ(𝐲j)-\frac{1}{2}q_j - \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)

Both are instances of Equation 8; the sign inversion is not a bug but the algebraic consequence of using the reciprocal weight.

3.4 Importance-Sampling Interpretation

The denominator ∑jexp⁡(−12qj−log⁡ĝ(𝐲j))\sum_j \exp(-\frac{1}{2}q_j - \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)) is equivalent to the Horvitz–Thompson estimator:

∫Mfd𝐱̂=1K∑j=1Kf(𝐲j)ĝ(𝐲j), \widehat{\int_M f\,d\mathbf{x}} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{j=1}^{K}\frac{f(\mathbf{y}_j)}{\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j)}, \tag{4}

which converges to ∫Mf(𝐱)d𝐱\int_M f(\mathbf{x})\,d\mathbf{x} as K→∞K \to \infty whenever ĝ(𝐲j)>0\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) > 0 for all jj in the support of ff (Horvitz and Thompson (1952); Hahn (1998)).

4 Implementation Call Chain 

optimize_niche(likelihood = "ip_weighted")
  └─ niche_obj.cpp::create_niche_obj_ptr()
       └─ loglik_niche_math_ip_weighted_eigen()   [C++, lines 101–154]
            ├─ build_L_cov()                       [theta → mu, sigma, L_cov]
            ├─ Mahalanobis q1 (occurrences), q2 (background)
            ├─ a_j = -0.5 * q2 - log_w_den         [line 143]
            ├─ logsumexp(a)                          [lines 145–147]
            ├─ neg_log = 0.5*sum_q1 + log_w_occ + n*lse
            └─ OPTIM_PENALTY guard                   [line 152]

4.1 Key Code (loglik_niche_math_cpp.cpp, lines 101–154)

The C++ kernel:

  1. Reconstructs LcovL_{\text{cov}} from θ\theta via build_L_cov() (line 123).
  2. Computes Mahalanobis distances for both occurrence and background points (lines 129–137).
  3. Clamps KDE weights: w.max(MIN_KDE_WEIGHT).log() with MIN_KDE_WEIGHT = 1e-300 to prevent log⁡(0)\log(0) (lines 141–142).
  4. Computes the integrand aj=−0.5qj−log⁡ĝ(𝐲j)a_j = -0.5 q_j - \log\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) (line 143).
  5. Evaluates logsumexp⁡(a)\operatorname{logsumexp}(a) via the max-shift trick (lines 145–147).
  6. Returns 0.5 * sum_q1 + log_w_occ.sum() + n * log_sum_exp (lines 149–151).

4.2 Analytic Gradient (lines 186–304)

The hybrid analytic/finite-difference gradient follows the same structure as the weighted gradient (see Model 2):

  • ∇μ\nabla_\mu: Closed-form via Σ−1[weighted mean shift]\Sigma^{-1}[\text{weighted mean shift}], with softmax weights πj=exp⁡(aj)/∑kexp⁡(ak)\pi_j = \exp(a_j)/\sum_k\exp(a_k) on the background side (lines 263–271).
  • ∇log⁡σk\nabla_{\log\sigma_k}: Closed-form via U⊙VU \odot V products (lines 273–278).
  • ∇vk\nabla_{v_k}: Central finite differences on the C-vine block (lines 280–298).

4.3 R Entry Point 

optimize_niche(env_occ, env_m, likelihood = "ip_weighted")

No ridge prior is applied by default because the IPW denominator provides natural self-regularisation (see Section 6).

5 KDE Computation

The KDE ĝ\hat{g} is computed identically to Model 2 (Scott’s rule bandwidth, Gaussian kernel, precomputed before optimisation). The only difference is that ĝ\hat{g} enters the likelihood with inverted sign:

  • In "weighted": the denominator uses +log⁡ĝ+\log\hat{g} (amplifying common environments).
  • In "ip_weighted": the denominator uses −log⁡ĝ-\log\hat{g} (down-weighting common environments).

6 Self-Regularisation

Unlike the weighted model, the IPW model does not require a ridge prior on log⁡σ\log\sigma to prevent σ→∞\sigma \to \infty. The mechanism:

  1. As σ→∞\sigma \to \infty, f(𝐲j)→constf(\mathbf{y}_j) \to \text{const} for all jj.
  2. The denominator becomes ∑jconst/ĝ(𝐲j)\sum_j \text{const}/\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j), which is large because 1/ĝ1/\hat{g} amplifies low-density tail points.
  3. Meanwhile the numerator ∏if(𝐱i)\prod_i f(\mathbf{x}_i) also flattens, but the denominator grows faster due to the tail amplification.
  4. The net effect is that −ℓ*-\ell^*increases as σ→∞\sigma \to \infty, providing a natural penalty.

This self-regularisation is a property of the Horvitz–Thompson estimator, not an ad hoc fix.

7 Limitations

  1. Variance amplification. When ĝ(𝐲j)≈0\hat{g}(\mathbf{y}_j) \approx 0 (environmental deserts), the weight 1/ĝ1/\hat{g} can be extremely large, inflating the variance of the estimator. Diagnostic: check the effective sample size ESS=(∑jwj)2/∑jwj2\text{ESS} = (\sum_j w_j)^2 / \sum_j w_j^2.

  2. KDE bandwidth sensitivity. Scott’s rule may under-smooth in low dimensions or over-smooth in high dimensions. Users should inspect the KDE fit.

  3. DGP mismatch. If presences are genuinely generated by the use-availability process (λ∝f⋅g\lambda \propto f \cdot g), then the IPW estimator targets the wrong quantity. Use "weighted" (Model 2) instead.

  4. Normality assumption. Same as Model 1. For asymmetric niches, consider combining IPW with a skew-normal or skew-t kernel (not yet implemented in nicher).

Jimenez, L., and J. Soberón. 2022. “Weighted Likelihood Estimation of the Fundamental Niche.” Ecological Modelling 470: 110009. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2022.110009.
